text:
sophie: Heads up — our us-west-2 GPU Savings Plan and several Reserved Instances are up for renewal in ~32 days. Utilization dipped below 65% last month, mostly on p3 -> p4g transition. thinking about whether to renew full term or pivot to a mixed plan. any thoughts?

james: Is the drop driven by seasonality or by model placement changes?

sophie: mostly placement — we moved a few heavy workloads to eu-west-1 for latency tests. also some job backfills moved to spot.

liam: Quick numbers: last 30d GPU-hours covered by commitments = 1,820h. billable on-demand = ~980h. effective coverage = 65%. (pulled from cost dashboard)

sophie: link to the quick view: https://redwood.console/finance/savings?region=us-west-2 : the shading shows p3 underused, p4 not enough reservations.

rita-finops: From billing side — current monthly committed spend for us-west-2 GPUs = $72k. If we renew same coverage for 1yr, monthly committed cost = $69k (small discount), projected op-ex vs on-demand ~15% savings assuming current usage. If we drop 25% of capacity we save ~ $17k/mo but risk throttle during spikes.

james: Could we do a convertible RI/compute savings plan mix to hedge instance family shifts? convertible RI gives flexibility but less discount vs standard.

liam: Ops angle: we can route non-latency-critical batch to spot or eu-west-1. For steady state inference traffic we should keep some base reserved capacity in us-west-2. Suggest: keep 60% coverage via 1yr savings plan (compute), and 20% as reserved convertible RI for family lock. rest on-demand/spot.

sophie: That sounds reasonable. What's the math if we convert 20% to convertible RI vs keep everything as savings plan?

rita-finops: Quick calc: 
- All savings plan 1yr: effective monthly = $58k (expected)
- 60% SP + 20% convertible RI + 20% on-demand: effective monthly = $61k but with lower risk.
Convertible RI up-front exposure slightly higher but allows instance family changes. I can run exact NPV numbers if you want.

james: Run an amortized 3yr vs 1yr scenario too — some teams prefer 3yr for deeper discount but we lose flexibility.

liam: Also flag: network egress from eu-west-1 back to us-west-2 increased cost when we moved models; if we keep cross-region routing for some jobs, net savings shrink. Need to add egress delta to cost model.

sophie: Good call. @rita-finops can you include egress delta in the calc and share a short table?

rita-finops: on it. I'll post a spreadsheet in ~2h. Will include sensitivity: 10/25/40% utilization drops, egress per-TB, and a break-even utilization threshold.

infra-bot: [reminder] Savings plan/RI renewal window opens in 29 days for resources in account:redwood-prod-usw2. Use /commitments tool to lock proposals.

james: Also: is there any chance AWS marketplace credits or partner discounts apply to the next renewal? last quarter we had one-off credits.

rita-finops: Checked — no standing credits remaining for us-west-2. We can negotiate with account rep for a multi-region commit if we consolidate. Might take 2-3 weeks to finalize.

liam: Operational ask: if we go with mixed strategy, ops needs a clear runbook for automatic fallbacks when reserved capacity is exhausted (route to spare pool in us-east-1 or burst into Dedicated). I'll draft during sprint.

sophie: ok let's do action items:
- rita-finops: post spreadsheet with 3 renewal scenarios + egress numbers (due in 2h)
- liam: draft fallback runbook and capacity routing config (due EOW)
- james: confirm if convertible RI is allowed across our Dedicated clusters / licensing (due tomorrow)
- sophie: schedule a quick sync in 48h to decide final commit amount

james: :thumbsup:

sophie: thanks everyone — ping me if anything surprising pops up.

infra-bot: thread archived after 7 days of inactivity.
